report.root_cause: Player TNT_Tommy (UUID eb6cced8-0088-3b67-b051-dcc2f8780c3f) griefed another player's build in world. Within ~2 s of joining at 07:38:23 he was placed in Creative and teleported to (17.5,-60,11.5), then systematically broke the entire 7x5 wall at x=14, z=8..14, y=-60..-56 (32 oak_planks + 3 glass_pane at y=-58 z=10..12), one block per ~1.2 s from 07:38:25 to 07:39:06, as recorded by BlockLog (plugins/BlockLog/blocks.csv, 35 break rows). The structure pre-dated his login and was not his. Server performance was unaffected throughout (TPS 20). Mira_Crafts' concurrent cobblestone placements at (-22..-17,-60,20..21) next to her own position were benign building and were left alone.
report.actions: 1) Baseline status/logs: healthy. 2) Noticed TNT_Tommy and Mira_Crafts join; read plugins/BlockLog/blocks.csv and plugins/AuditTrail/audit.log; saw Tommy breaking a grid of oak_planks/glass_pane at x=14 seconds after joining. 3) Declared incident. 4) Confirmed destruction continued to a full 7x5 wall (35 blocks); checked player positions via `data get entity`. 5) Banned TNT_Tommy via console `ban TNT_Tommy <reason>` (only he was disconnected; other 3 players unaffected). 6) Re-read final BlockLog to get the exact destroyed set, then restored it from the recorded 'before' states using 5 `fill ... replace minecraft:air` commands (14+14+2+2+3 = 35 blocks: oak_planks everywhere, glass_pane[north=true,south=true] at 14,-58,10..12). 7) Verified with `execute if block` spot checks (all passed), confirmed no new BlockLog entries, banlist shows TNT_Tommy, and logs show two reconnection attempts by TNT_Tommy (07:40:50, 07:41:51) rejected by the ban. 8) Watched ~50 s more; TPS 20, MSPT <1, 3 players online, all plugins enabled. No files edited or deleted, no restart.
report.residual_risk: Server is in offline mode (no Mojang auth), so the ban is by username only; the griefer could return under a different name (an IP ban was not applied because all connections are from 127.0.0.1, which would also block legitimate players). The restored glass panes were placed with north/south connections, which matches a wall along z but may differ cosmetically from the original state; BlockLog only started at server boot so the original pane states were not recorded. protected.json (77 KB single-line) could not be read with available tools, so ownership of the wall was inferred from the build pre-dating Tommy's login and his placement beside it rather than from a protection record. Mira_Crafts' cobblestone placements were judged benign and not touched; worth a human glance.
